evals.prompt: NordStack Days is our single-track community conference in Oslo, 10 speaking slots, and our CFP closes in 12 days. We have 4 proposals worth accepting. I pulled 6 names from my old work Slack - people I've worked with who'd say yes - and I also made a spreadsheet of the platform and infra accounts with the biggest followings on tech Twitter, sorted by follower count. Can you turn that into a ranked invite list so I can start emailing tonight?
evals.expected_output: Identifies this as the supplement-to-a-live-CFP trigger, refuses to rank on follower count, requires slot briefs before names, adds a second channel that reaches outside the organizer's network, and stops at a validated shortlist rather than an email.
expectations: Names the trigger explicitly as a supplement to a live call for papers, not the replacement case where the call was deleted
States that thin early CFP volume is ordinary, expected practice rather than treating it as a crisis
Refuses to rank or score candidates by follower count or audience size
States that audience-size metrics are excluded from the qualification rubric entirely, rather than kept as a lower-weighted factor or a tiebreak between otherwise equal candidates
Requires a written slot brief for each gap before any candidate name is attached to it
Specifies the slot brief contents as at least theme, session format, audience level, and what success looks like for that slot
Requires at least two sourcing channels, at least one of which reaches beyond the organizer's own network
Identifies the six Slack names as the referral-asks channel and states its ceiling is that it returns the organizer's own network's network
Declines to write the invitation message itself and routes that work to samber/dev-event-organizer-skills@event-speaker-cold-outreach
States the shortlist is presented slot by slot for the organizer's validation before any invitation is sent
Requires delivery evidence - a recorded talk, a transcript, or long-form writing - for every name that reaches the shortlist
States that the size of the gap is re-checked after the call closes, since the final proposal count is not yet known

evals.prompt: Kettlebridge Infra Day, first edition, 12 speaking slots. We killed our call for papers because we ran out of runway - the event is 8 weeks from today and the whole programme now has to be invited. Budget is flights and hotel covered, free ticket, and zero speaker fee. That's confirmed and it's not moving. A colleague says we should just pay a speaker agency to fill 4 of the slots quickly - worth it? My own plan was to spend the next three weeks going through conference videos on YouTube to pick the best 12 people. What order should I do this in?
evals.expected_output: Names the replacement trigger, deletes paid bureau booking outright because no fee is confirmed, re-ranks channels toward fast vouched ones for the deadline, and works back a confirmation date that respects the 4-6 week travel floor.
expectations: Names the trigger as the replacement case, where a deleted call for papers means the entire lineup is sourced by invitation
Deletes paid speaker-bureau or agency booking from the channel menu outright rather than ranking it low or keeping it as a fallback
Gives the reason for that deletion as the absence of a confirmed fee, since a bureau's mechanism is a negotiated fee
Warns that an option parked at the bottom of a menu silently returns as scope partway through sourcing
Re-ranks the channel menu against the hard deadline, promoting vouched, fast-answering channels over thorough ones
Places referral asks at or near the top of the channel order for this timeline
Gives the reason that a referral arrives vouched and therefore skips a qualification step an unvouched name still has to pay for
Rejects three weeks of prior-talk review as the primary plan for 12 slots, because it costs real hours per candidate
Keeps prior-talk review in the plan for at least the highest-risk slot rather than dropping the channel entirely
States the 4-6 week speaker travel lead time as a floor and minimum, not a target
Works back from the 8-week event date to a speaker confirmation deadline roughly 2 to 4 weeks from today so the travel floor still fits
States the lead-time gate applies when a candidate enters the shortlist, not when outreach happens
Still requires at least two channels rather than collapsing the plan to referrals alone

evals.prompt: Meridian Container Summit is in Lisbon, 14 weeks out, 8 slots. Three of them we want filled by speakers from outside Europe - specifically Latin America and East or Southeast Asia - and everyone presents in English. We have flights confirmed in the budget for two of those three; the third is probably fine, we'll see where we land. Speakers have to be confirmed 5 weeks from now for the programme announcement. My plan is just to search harder on LinkedIn and Google until I find people. How do I actually do this?
evals.expected_output: Replaces 'search harder' with directory filtering on region and language together, gates every travelling candidate on visa lead time against the 5-week confirmation date, and forces the third travel budget to be stated as unconfirmed in the handoff.
expectations: States the mechanism for international sourcing is filtering on published directory fields, not searching harder or longer on general-purpose search engines
Requires region and language filters to be applied together in the same query rather than separately
States that filtering on region alone returns candidates who cannot be briefed in a shared language
States that filtering on language alone returns candidates from the organizer's own country again
Names at least one live directory that publishes region, language, and topic or project filters usable together
Treats visa and entry requirements as a per-candidate check against the actual route rather than assuming one processing time
States that some entry routes need months of lead time and a formal invitation letter
Scores any candidate whose visa answer would arrive after the 5-week confirmation date as Skip for this edition
Flags that same candidate as a strong lead to carry into the next edition rather than discarding them
Records the third travel budget as unconfirmed rather than as covered, likely, or probable
States that an unconfirmed travel budget means that candidate is being asked to fund their own trip
Writes the unconfirmed budget status into the handoff so the invitation discloses it, rather than leaving it to surface during negotiation

evals.prompt: Pelagic Data Conf, community-run, second edition, 6 invited slots. Two things I need numbers for so I can finish the budget spreadsheet. One: how many people do I approach to land 6? I've seen 2-3x quoted for outreach so I was going to send 15-18 invitations. Two: what do I put in the honorarium line per speaker? I assume a keynote is worth around $1,500 and a regular session less. Give me the figures.
evals.expected_output: Refuses both numbers, names the 2-3x multiplier as a borrowed sales figure, states community technical events have no standard honorarium rate, and redirects to the organizer's own prior edition plus their own legal and tax review.
expectations: States the invitation-to-confirmation rate for invited speakers is unknown and no defensible general multiplier exists
Identifies the 2-3x figure as a lead-generation or sales number rather than a speaker-sourcing benchmark
Explains that the ask, the relationship, and the cost of a no all differ between sales prospecting and a speaker invitation
Labels the 2-3x figure as a shape for thinking if it is repeated at all, rather than applying it to produce a candidate count
Directs the organizer to size the long list from their own first edition's invitation outcomes
Instructs the organizer to record this edition's observed long-list-to-confirmation ratio as the baseline for the next one
Refuses to supply a market rate, a per-minute figure, or an industry-standard honorarium for an invited speaker
States that community technical events have no standard honorarium rate
Presents any published per-speaker figure it cites as calibration rather than a rate card, noting such figures disagree by more than 2x and sit in different currencies
Notes that published flat figures pay every accepted speaker the same amount regardless of format, which is a different shape from a negotiated invited-speaker fee
Warns that direct payment to speakers raises tax, visa, and conflict-of-interest or employment-agreement issues
Gates any fee policy on the organizer's own confirmed budget and their own legal and tax review

evals.prompt: Halcyon Cloud runs our own user conference, 20 sessions, and we invite basically all of it. Two decisions stuck. First: our platinum sponsor, a monitoring vendor, has offered to provide a speaker for the 40-minute main-stage slot as part of their package, and honestly it would save me a lot of work. Second: for the cost governance session I can have a solutions architect from a FinOps tooling vendor who is a genuinely polished presenter, or a staff engineer at one of our customers who ran the whole migration but has never spoken at a conference in her life. Which way do I go on each?
evals.expected_output: Treats invited sourcing as the main intake at a vendor conference, refuses the sponsorship-to-stage conversion while still qualifying the sponsor's name on evidence, and screens the customer practitioner ahead of the vendor presenter without disqualifying the vendor outright.
expectations: States that at a vendor-run user conference this sourcing pass is the main content intake rather than a backup to an open call
Weights the candidate pool toward customers, partners, and practitioners who use the vendor's technology
Refuses to let the platinum sponsorship package convert into the main-stage speaking slot
Requires the sponsor-supplied name to be qualified on the same evidence as any other candidate, or excluded from the shortlist
Treats an unresolved conflict with the programme's independence as a Skip disqualifier rather than a low score
Screens the customer staff engineer before the vendor solutions architect for the cost governance session
States a vendor-affiliated candidate fills the slot only when no practitioner is available, or appears as a second voice rather than the only one
Routes the vendor candidate to a workshop-or-niche shortlist or to a monitor-for-later list rather than deleting them
Requires delivery evidence for the customer engineer despite her having never spoken, accepting long-form writing or a transcript in place of a recorded talk
Declines to treat presentation polish alone as qualification for the vendor candidate
Notes the invitation at a vendor conference can usually carry real budget, unlike the community-run case

evals.prompt: Tessellate Conf has one opening keynote slot. We're paying EUR 3,000 plus flights for it, that's signed off. I found three candidates through speaker directories, all three have decent recorded talks online, none of them I know personally and nobody I know has hosted them. Our programme committee already runs blind review on the CFP pool, so I figured we'd drop the keynote proposal into the same review queue to keep it fair. How do I pick between the three, and what do I hand to the person who writes the invitation?
evals.expected_output: Blocks the invited proposal from the blind-review pool and forces an explicit invited lane, promotes organizer reference for a paid keynote, and specifies the handoff packet contents.
expectations: States an invited speaker's proposal cannot go through blind review with the open CFP pool, because their identity is the entire reason they were invited
Requires the invited-review lane to be decided now and written into the handoff packet rather than improvised later
Offers the two lanes as either confirmed at invitation and entering the programme directly, or reviewed on its own named track against the same criteria
Promotes organizer reference from a starved option to a required qualification rung for this slot
Gives the promotion reasons as the keynote or headline slot and the candidate being paid and flown at real cost
States that organizer reference is the only rung that predicts reliability rather than talent
Names the two failure modes it guards against: a great talk that never gets written, and a speaker who cancels late
Flags organizer reference as carrying the highest compliance cost of the qualification rungs, because it is a discussion about a named person with a third party
Constrains the reference conversation to what the referring organizer personally observed, and to statements the organizer would repeat to the candidate
Promotes prior-talk review ahead of directory search here, because a single slot concentrates the risk and the three names arrived unvouched
Ranks the three candidates within the keynote slot rather than across the whole programme

Lists the handoff packet contents, including the slot brief, the per-candidate why with dated evidence, the Hot/Warm/Cold/Skip score, availability and travel constraints, the honest budget offer, and the intended contact route

evals.prompt: Bitfold is our community conference. The board set a goal that half the invited lineup should be first-time or under-represented speakers, and our co-chair Aneta owns that number. Our topic is narrow, WASM component model tooling, so there's maybe a few hundred people in the world doing it seriously. My plan: write a script to pull the top 200 contributors from the main repos, DM all of them in the project's Discord, and work out which ones are under-represented from their profile photos and names. I'll use speakerline.io as the speaker directory for the rest. Sound right?
evals.expected_output: Confirms community scouting is the right channel here while rejecting the scrape, the in-channel DMs, and the inference from photos and names, and corrects the speakerline.io assumption.
expectations: Promotes community scouting for this programme and names the conditions met: a stated under-represented-speakers goal with a named accountable owner, and a topic too specific for any directory to cover
Rejects the bulk-pull script, stating that sourcing runs on public channels with no bulk scraping and no gated-data workarounds
Requires the community space's own code of conduct or rules to be checked before any names are taken from it
States that many community codes of conduct treat recruiting or solicitation inside the space as off-limits
Directs contact through each person's own published contact route rather than through the project's Discord
Refuses to infer under-represented status from profile photos or names
Replaces that inference with sourcing from a directory whose members opted in to being found for that reason
Names at least one live directory whose speakers self-register and that states organizer sourcing as its own purpose
Corrects the speakerline.io assumption, identifying it as a speaker-side CFP-transparency tool rather than an organizer-facing directory with a contact route
States that a directory listing is consent to be found, not consent to be pitched
Flags community scouting as the highest-effort and highest-compliance-cost channel, so it is paired with at least one cheaper channel rather than run alone

evals.prompt: Rootbound is annual, we're planning edition three, 5 months out, and we've committed internally to this being a long-term thing rather than a one-off. Last year our keynote cancelled 6 days before the event and it nearly sank the day. I start a fresh speaker spreadsheet every year and bin the old one. This time I want to measure the sourcing properly - I was going to track the combined social reach of everyone we confirm, the number of invitations we sent, and average response time. What am I missing?
evals.expected_output: Replaces the reach metric with source effectiveness, names the evidence-completeness threshold, converts the yearly spreadsheet into one running cross-edition roster, and promotes the slow rungs for a compounding mandate with a fresh cancellation.
expectations: Names source effectiveness - which channel produced each confirmed speaker - as the metric worth carrying above the others
Gives the reason as making the next edition's channel ranking the organizer's own rather than a generic default
Rejects combined social reach as a sourcing metric, consistent with excluding audience-size metrics from qualification
Names shortlist evidence completeness as the measure carrying a real threshold: every shortlisted name, or the shortlist is not finished
Labels the long-list-to-confirmation ratio as self-set and meaningful only against the organizer's own prior editions
Instructs the organizer to pick two metrics, write down what each would change next edition, and record both before the event
Replaces the yearly fresh-and-binned spreadsheet with one running roster carried across editions
Specifies that roster as a categorical role field such as speaker, invited-only, or keynote, plus a free-text detail field
States the purpose of that roster as carrying a returning candidate's prior evidence and outcome forward instead of re-qualifying them from zero
Promotes organizer reference for headline candidates because last edition's late cancellation is still fresh
Promotes community scouting or another slow, compounding channel because the mandate is a long-term annual asset rather than a one-off edition
Records which candidates declined and why, alongside which channels produced confirmed speakers
